prompt: Assemble a nested explorer: a BorderLayout panel whose CENTER holds a horizontal JSplitPane, with a BoxLayout button column in the left scroll pane and a text area in the right one.
explanation: Real layouts are trees, not single containers: each level picks the layout manager that suits it, so BorderLayout stretches the split pane, the split pane divides the space, and BoxLayout stacks the buttons in a column. A JScrollPane does not contain its view directly -- it puts it inside a JViewport, which is why tests reach the nav panel through getViewport().getView(). BoxLayout is the one layout manager that needs its container passed to the constructor, because it measures that container as it lays components out.
hints: new BoxLayout(nav, BoxLayout.Y_AXIS) -- BoxLayout is unusual in needing the container itself.
new JScrollPane(view) wraps a component; give each scroll pane its name with setName before adding it.
The JSplitPane(orientation, left, right) constructor takes both sides at once, then add it with BorderLayout.CENTER.
